Question:
Use `tests/qa/testcase.py`, class `TestTemplateSearchDeepKeysMaxCallDepthQA`, method `test_template_search_deep_keys_max_call_depth_case`. The test instantiates `cfnlint.template.template.Template("foo.yaml", _TEMPLATE, ["us-east-1"])`. `Template.__init__` invokes `self.search_deep_keys(...)` FIVE TIMES -- once each for the searchTexts "Ref", "Fn::Sub", "Fn::If", "Fn::FindInMap", and `FUNCTION_FOR_EACH` (a `re.Pattern`). Each `search_deep_keys` invocation calls `Template._search_deep_keys(searchText, self.template, [])` once on the template ROOT and (if `includeGlobals=True` and Globals exist) once on `self.transform_pre["Globals"]`; in this run Globals is `{}`, so the second call enters the empty-dict branch and adds only depth 1. The private `_search_deep_keys` (lines 351-399 of `src/cfnlint/template/template.py`) recurses by these rules: (a) DICT cfndict: iterate keys; for each key, recurse on its value ONLY IF the value is a dict or a list. Scalar values (str/int/float/None) do NOT trigger a recursive call. (b) LIST cfndict: iterate items and recurse on EVERY item, regardless of type (string items just bottom-out without further recursion). (c) DICT cfndict whose key has a LIST value: recursion is per list item (depth +1 per item), NOT a single +1 for the list. Restricting the call-stack depth count to ONLY frames whose qualified name is `cfnlint.template.template.Template._search_deep_keys`, what is the MAXIMUM simultaneous depth of in-flight frames reached during this test run? Return the answer under the field `maximum_call_stack_depth`.

`Template.__init__` calls `search_deep_keys` five times for the five search texts named in the question. Each `search_deep_keys` makes one `_search_deep_keys(..., self.template, [])` call on the root and, because `includeGlobals` defaults to `True`, one more `_search_deep_keys(..., self.transform_pre["Globals"], [])` call; since `Globals` is `{}`, that second call contributes only a single in-flight frame.

So the maximum comes from the deepest recursion during one root search. In `_search_deep_keys`, dict values recurse only when the value is a dict or list, while list handling recurses on every item and adds one frame per nested list/item level. In the test template, the deepest chain is:
root template dict → `"Resources"` dict → `"Bucket"` dict → `"Properties"` dict → `"Tags"` list item at index 1 (outer nested list) → its index 0 item (inner nested list) → its index 0 item (dict `{"Inner": ...}`) → `"Inner"` dict value → `"Tag"` dict value.
That is 9 simultaneous `_search_deep_keys` frames. The leaf `{"Key": "k", "Value": "v"}` is the 9th frame and does not recurse further because its values are scalars.
